hints.title: Tallest First Line Insertion Strategy
hints.text: Taller people do not see shorter people in front of them. How can arranging taller people first simplify inserting each person at their exact required position in line?

hints.title: Relative Height Independence Invariant
hints.text: Inserting people in descending order of height means each newly inserted person only considers already-placed people who are at least as tall.

hints.title: Descending Height Index Insertion Procedure
hints.text: Sort people in descending order by height, breaking ties by ascending k value. Initialize an empty list. Insert each person into the list at index equal to their k value. Return the reconstructed list.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input array length or bit count
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all permutations to satisfy relative counts requires O(N!) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting and list insertion places N elements in O(N^2) time using O(N) output storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that sorting by (-height, k) decouples the problem so each element can be greedily placed at index k.
